department: Department of Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering

deadline.value: Apply by December 1, 2026, 23:59 Pacific; the deadline is strictly observed (Fall entry only).

gre_general.value: The General GRE is required for the 2027-28 cycle.

also.quote: (Note that the GRE is required for the 2027–2028 admissions cycle.)

fee_waiver.value: The MAE department offers no application fee waivers.
fee_waiver.quote: The UCLA Department of Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering (MAE) does not offer graduate application fee waivers.

supervisor.value: Applicants name a preferred faculty advisor; students admitted without a master's become Ph.D. students only after passing the preliminary exam and securing a faculty advisor's commitment.
supervisor.quote: Applicants must select a field of study and preferred faculty advisor when submitting the online application. | Students may later petition to change their classification to the Ph.D. program after successfully passing both parts of the Ph.D. preliminary examination and obtaining the commitment of an MAE faculty advisor to provide research supervision

funding.value: No support should be expected unless offered in writing; research assistantships from individual faculty are the main source, and fellowships go to exceptional applicants.
funding.quote: Unless you have been officially notified in writing of an award from the department or the Graduate Division, you should not expect any financial support from UCLA. | Graduate student research positions are awarded directly by individual faculty. This is the most common form of financial assistance.

entry_route.value: Direct Ph.D. admission is for master's holders; bachelor's-only applicants are normally admitted to the M.S. and petition to move to the Ph.D.
entry_route.quote: The Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering (MAE) Graduate Program offers direct admission to the Ph.D. program to applicants who have already earned a master’s degree. Graduate applicants without a master’s degree are normally admitted to the M.S. program.

notes: Aerospace Engineering is a separate Ph.D. major in the same department with the same admissions page.
